summary: Verdict: fix_first. Scope: I checked the 18 highest-scoring plants (ranks 14-18 tie at 55) and ran my own scripts over all 66 profiled plants. Method: (a) fetch_page.py --check on every stated row cited by a score row or opening line of those 18 plants (about 120 quote/URL pairs): all found except three that need browser navigation (Universal's Paylocity list, confirmed by browser; two Grid Structures rows, see evidence-10); (b) live re-fetch of every posting behind a labor 12 or 20 in the top 18; (c) parent job boards queried directly (Arcosa UKG board, Crest Lever API, Tallo listings for Sabre); (d) a rubric script over all six components, confidence, tiers and totals. What holds up: arithmetic, tier thresholds and score-row values reproduce with 0 errors; quotes are on their pages and name the right plant; the postings behind Maico, Universal, DIS-TRAN, MICA, Meyer Tulsa, Crowley, Nello, West Hazleton, Grid, PennFab, Millerbernd and Western Utility Telecom are live today; Meyer Tulsa's Feb 27, 2026 trigger and FCAW rows (never fact-checked before) verify; twelve of fifteen demand-15 triggers are dated plant-level events inside the 24-month window; tiers (OEM / Contract fabricator / Tier 1) fit the definitions; the map was built from the current ledger. What does not: (1) labor is wrong for at least eleven plants of two multi-plant parents. Arcosa's own job board, which the ledger already cites for Meyer Tulsa, shows open dated welder postings at eight Arcosa plants that the map reports as '0 open' or 'none found' (Meyer Clinton becomes High at 75; six others move 48 -> 68), and live Sabre postings exist for Alvarado, Sioux City and Hicksville (Alvarado 28 -> 68). The ranking and the top-10 list are materially wrong until this is fixed. (2) The number 1 plant, Millerbernd Winsted, is Path's published case-study account but carries a cold opening line and the label customer_other_plant. (3) Material 12 at DiHighway and Race Rock Brookshire contradicts the coordinator's own rulings on Muskogee and PennFab; both drop to Low. (4) Confidence is computed unevenly (the vertical-level demand 8 counts for 40 of 51 plants and not the other 11). (5) Three demand-15 scores rest on a hiring event or a company-level ownership change. (6) Relationship and owner fields: HW Metals is not a direct competitor lookalike; lookalike_of uses three formats; Sabre, Sovereign, two Meyer plants and Hapco carry stale or inconsistent owner text; the Hicksville plant is still named FWT, LLC on 2015 evidence; a 2017 headcount scores scale 10. Not checked: plants below rank 18 were covered by the scripts and spot checks only; Valmont's own careers site returned 502, so labor 0 at the seven Valmont plants is untested against a primary board; Nucor sibling plants were not re-pulled; FWT Fort Worth's current status is unresolved; closing of the TPG-Sabre deal could not be confirmed. If evidence-1 to evidence-6 are applied, expect roughly: High 4 -> 5 (Clinton in; Crowley stays or drops per evidence-7), and eight to ten Medium plants reordered.

findings.finding: The top-ranked plant on the map (88, High) is Path's own published case-study customer, yet it is labelled customer_other_plant ('same parent, not reported as converted') and its opening line is a cold pitch ('how are you covering pole welding capacity?') that never mentions the Path cells. The record contradicts itself: existing_robots says 'yes: Path welding cells', and the material score of 20 is earned only because 'Path cells fabricate Millerbernd's T&I poles'. An SDR who uses this line on an existing account will look uninformed. The ledger's own facts make Winsted the converted site: Path's page names T&I poles, and the ledger excludes Millerbernd's other two campuses (595 Industrial Dr and Sauk Rapids) as circular-products plants that do not make poles.
findings.evidence: https://www.path-robotics.com/videos/case-study-millerbernd (fetched 2026-11-13): 'Hear how Millerbernd has leveraged Path's intelligent welding cells to fabricate Transportation & Infrastructure poles.' Ledger rows: p-millerbernd-winsted-mn:relationship = customer_other_plant (coordinator 'strict rule'); :existing_robots = 'yes: Path welding cells ... attributed to the Winsted main campus because T&I poles are made there'; :score_material_part reasoning cites the Path page. Lead, not a quote: two web searches on 2026-11-13 returned summaries of Millerbernd postings for a 'Path Cell Robotics Automation Technician' on the 'Transportation & Infrastructure (Pole) team' in Winsted (career.com posting 3/17/2025; factoryfix automation-technician-weekend-shift--winsted--mn--1638672135 and tealhq copies now return 410/closed), which would be a primary source naming the plant.
findings.fix: Mechanical minimum (no rule change): rewrite the opening line as an account-expansion line that acknowledges the existing Path cells (e.g. which pole weldments still go through manual GMAW or the sub-arc seam station), and flag the plant on the map and in the top-10 list as an existing Path account so it does not head the cold-call list. Rule decision for the coordinator (it overrides the logged strict rule, since Millerbernd has three welding sites): set relationship = known_customer, tag inferred, reasoning 'Path names Millerbernd's T&I poles and the ledger shows T&I poles are made only at the Winsted main campus', i.e. extend the single-site exception to 'single site for the named product'. Research: retrieve an archived or live copy of the 'Path Cell Robotics Automation Technician' posting and add it as a stated row for existing_robots and relationship. Apply the same wording check to Nello South Bend (FAT passed; line is acceptable) and the Valmont plants (line for p-valmont-tulsa-ok asks 'could an autonomous cell add welding capacity' of a company whose 2021 statement says Path is on its factory floors; add the caveat).

findings.finding: Confidence is not comparable between plants. (a) Demand 8 (vertical outlook only, no plant fact) adds 1 to confidence for 40 of the 51 plants at demand 8 and 0 for the other 11, depending only on whether the profiler happened to also cite the plant's (unknown) triggers claim in the score row. (b) tools/normalise_scores.py treats a claim_id as stated if any row under it is stated, so a component counts even when the row that carries the rubric fact is inferred. Millerbernd shows confidence 5, but its labor 20 ('several postings at once') rests on two inferred welder_postings rows (the stated rows under that claim_id are the shift pattern and '4x10 work week, optional overtime'), and its material 20 rests on an inferred existing_robots row. Western Utility Telecom's labor 12 rests on an inferred careers-page row; the stated row is the shift list of a posting that expired in June 2026.
findings.evidence: My script (scratchpad check.py, comp analysis) recomputed every plant: totals, tiers and the normaliser's own confidence rule all reproduce (0 arithmetic errors across 66 plants). Demand-8 plants where demand is NOT counted: p-meyer-steele-al, p-meyer-hager-city-wi, p-meyer-fort-worth-tx, p-meyer-lancaster-sc, p-browning-enterprise-attalla-al, p-arcosa-traffic-structures-sumterville-fl, p-ameron-tulsa-ok, p-arcosa-telecom-muskogee-ok, p-pennfab-morrisville-pa, p-metal-pros-wichita-ks, p-dihighway-new-york-mills-ny; counted for the other 40 (e.g. p-brookfield-brookfield-mo has confidence 1 from demand 8 alone). Millerbernd welder_postings rows: tags inferred, inferred, stated ('4x10 week with optional overtime'), stated ('shifts: 1st, 2nd and weekend'). Also: five Meyer plants' score_scale rows cite '<id>:headcount', a claim_id with no evidence row.
findings.fix: (1) Mechanical, in normalise_scores.py: a demand score of 8 never counts toward confidence (it is not plant evidence). This lowers the 40 plants listed as 'counted' by 1 and makes the figure uniform (Millerbernd, Maico, DIS-TRAN Pineville, MICA Haltom City, Universal and Western Utility Telecom 5 -> 4; Crowley and Meyer Tulsa unchanged because their demand is 15 on stated triggers). (2) By hand for the two cases found: Millerbernd labor and material and Western Utility Telecom labor do not count until their carrying rows are stated (Millerbernd 4 -> 3 if only labor is fixed via evidence-13's Tallo rows, Western Utility Telecom 4 -> 3). (3) Going forward, have each score row name the specific evidence row (claim_id plus source_url) it relies on, and count the component only if that row is stated; do not use an 'all rows under the claim are stated' test, which would penalise plants with extra inferred context rows (Meyer Tulsa would fall from 4 to 1). Remove the five dangling '<id>:headcount' citations. State the rule on the Method page.

findings.fix: p-valmont-tulsa-ok: set score_demand = 8 (55 -> 48, still Medium), move the hiring event into welder_postings as a dated past event (labor stays 0 unless a live posting is found), and drop it from the opening line or date it clearly. p-nello-spring-grove-mn and p-nello-westby-wi: set score_demand = 8 (35 -> 28 each, Low unchanged), or find a dated plant-level source for the Westby opening (month in 2024/2025) or the announced investment.

findings.area: process rule wording and evidence rows
findings.finding: The run_log rule says process 20 needs MIG or flux-core 'named as a requirement in a welder or fitter posting'. Five plants hold 20 on a preferred or desired qualification in a welder posting (Grid: listed under 'DESIRED EDUCATION, KNOWLEDGE, AND/OR SKILLS' while the ledger value says 'required'; West Hazleton: under 'Preferred Qualifications'; Sabre Sioux City: 'preferred'; Meyer Hager City and Ameron 66th St: 'highly preferred'). The later log line ('a process named in a welder posting for the plant = 20') covers them, so the scores are consistent with each other, but the written rule and one value are not. PennFab's only stated weld_processes row quotes a sentence that names no process ('We at PennFab use this process due to the high deposition rates ...').
findings.evidence: Fetched 2026-11-13: jobs.nucor.com West Hazleton Fitter Welder page: 'Date: Oct 27, 2026', 'Preferred Qualifications: ... 2. Mig Flux core Welding Experience'. Grid careers page (secure7.saashr.com/ta/6215176.careers, page 2 of 2): 'Welder (Day & Night Shift) ... Amite, LA' still listed. p-grid-structures-amite-city-la:weld_processes value 'flux-core (FCAW) required in Amite welder posting'. The two Grid quotes ('1-2 years welding experience with some flux core welding (FCAW)' and 'Welder (Day & Night Shift) Apply Amite, LA Welder $27.00 - $31.00 / Hour') do not reproduce from the cited URL with fetch_page.py --check: the list is paged (28 jobs, the welder role is on page 2) and the FCAW line sits in a detail view. On page 2 I saw the title and 'Amite, LA' but could not confirm the pay line for the Welder role; on page 1 the $27.00 - $31.00 pay appears on 'Fitter (Day & Night Shift)'. The opening line quotes '$27-$31 an hour' for the welder opening.
findings.fix: Restate the rule in run_log as 'MIG/flux-core named (required or preferred) in a welder or fitter posting for this plant, or stated by the plant; a preferred item in a non-welding role does not count'. Change the Grid value to 'flux-core (FCAW) listed under desired skills in the Amite welder posting'; cite the posting's own detail URL for both Grid rows, re-confirm the welder pay range there, and correct the opening line if the $27-$31 figure belongs to the Fitter role. PennFab: replace the quote with the page's sentence that names gas metal arc / flux core, or cite the careers line 'Must have MIG welding experience.'
